name: cascade-mtg
description: Ask about your Magic: The Gathering collection, decks, lists and card prices in your Cascade account, and add or remove cards if you allow it.

interface.longDescription:
Cascade is a Magic: The Gathering collection manager for the web, Windows, iOS and Android. This plugin lets ChatGPT read your own Cascade account, so you can ask about your cards in plain language. If you allow it, ChatGPT can also make changes for you. It is for Magic players who keep their collection and decks in Cascade.

What you can ask about:
- Collection: search your cards by name, color, type, set, rarity or deck use, and see the total value and your most valuable cards.
- Decks: open a deck, and see which cards you own, which are missing, and which are in use by other decks.
- Lists: read your lists, wishlist, watchlist and binders.
- Prices: look up any card, with its printings, its TCGplayer prices in US dollars and its price history, and see which of your cards moved most.
- Meta decks: see which archetypes from recent MTGO decklists you can build with the cards you own.
- Set completion: see your progress in each set and the cards that you are missing.

What ChatGPT can change, only if you allow it:
- Add cards to your collection, wishlist, watchlist, lists and decks.
- Create lists, decks and binders, and move cards between binders.
- Remove cards from your collection, wishlist, watchlist, lists and decks. This is a second permission. ChatGPT never deletes a list, deck or binder.
- Undo a change. You can also undo each change on your Cascade account page.

Results link to the matching pages on Cascade.

Limitations: ChatGPT only reads your data until you turn on the switch that lets it make changes, and it removes cards only after you also turn on the switch that lets it remove cards. Both switches are off at the start. You find them on the Cascade page that opens when you connect, and later under “Connected apps” on your Cascade account page. The plugin cannot buy or sell cards. It cannot see your email address, your payments or your support messages. You need a Cascade account. Some results depend on your Cascade plan.

Magic: The Gathering is a trademark of Wizards of the Coast LLC. Cascade is not affiliated with or endorsed by Wizards of the Coast LLC.
defaultPrompt: What is my Magic collection worth, and which cards are the most valuable?
Which cards am I missing for my Commander deck, and what do they cost?
Which Modern meta decks can I build with the cards I own?

positive.description: Collection value and the most valuable cards
positive.prompt: What is my Magic collection worth, and which cards are the most valuable?
positive.expected_behavior: Gives the total value in US dollars, the card count and the most valuable printings, with The One Ring and Ragavan near the top, and names TCGplayer as the price source.

positive.description: Missing cards of a deck, with prices
positive.prompt: Which cards am I missing for my Krenko Goblins deck, and what do they cost?
positive.expected_behavior: Names Cavern of Souls, Kiki-Jiki, Mirror Breaker, Goblin Lackey and Goblin Recruiter as the missing cards, with their prices in US dollars.

positive.prompt: How far am I in completing Foundations?
positive.expected_behavior: Gives how many cards of Foundations the account owns out of the set total, and can name cards that are missing.

positive.description: Meta decks that the owned cards can build
positive.prompt: Which Modern meta decks can I build with the cards I own?
positive.expected_behavior: Lists archetypes from recent MTGO decklists with their meta share and how much of each deck the account owns, and names MTGO as the source.

positive.description: One card: its price and the owned copies, in two languages
positive.prompt: How much is Sheoldred, the Apocalypse worth, and do I own it?
positive.expected_behavior: Gives the prices of its printings in US dollars and says that the account owns an English copy and a Japanese copy.

positive.description: A change and its undo (needs “Can make changes” on for the connection)
positive.prompt: Add one Goblin Guide to my wishlist, then undo that change.
positive.expected_behavior: Adds one Goblin Guide to the wishlist and says so, then undoes the change, so the wishlist ends as it was.

positive.description: A removal and its undo (needs “Can make changes” and “Can remove cards” on for the connection)
positive.prompt: Remove one Mountain from my collection, then undo that change.
positive.expected_behavior: Confirms the card and the quantity, removes one Mountain from the collection, then undoes the change, so the collection ends as it was.

negative.description: The request has no relation to a Magic collection, so the plugin must not be used. ChatGPT answers without a Cascade tool.
negative.prompt: What will the weather be in Seattle tomorrow?

negative.description: The plugin has no tool that sells or buys cards. No tool call sells anything. ChatGPT can show the price and must say that it cannot sell the card.
negative.prompt: Sell my The One Ring on TCGplayer for the best price.

negative.description: Every tool works only on the data of the signed-in user. ChatGPT must say that it cannot show the collection of another user, and it returns no data of another user.
negative.prompt: Show me the collection of another Cascade user.

review.commerce_description: This plugin does not sell products or process payments.

publication.release_notes: ChatGPT can now make changes in your Cascade account when you allow it: add cards to your collection, wishlist, watchlist, lists and decks, create lists, decks and binders, move cards between binders, remove cards, and undo a change. Both permissions are off until you turn them on.
